title: Laplace posterior over Mirror coordinates only
hypothesis: A Laplace posterior over a low-dimensional Mirror code preserves quality/calibration at lower complete bytes than full last-layer Laplace and improves over native subspace/diagonal controls.
physical_object: frozen random-feature network and MAP output weights
mirror_coordinate: stochastic low-dimensional output-weight View code with code-space Hessian
logical_multiplicity: posterior predictive samples from one frozen feature network

development.selection_metric: test predictive NLL, accuracy, ECE, complete posterior bytes

fresh.reason: no audit after exact native subspace alias or frozen quality failure

storage.authority: actual serialized inference posterior payload bytes

success_gate: NLL delta <=.02, accuracy delta <=.01, ECE delta <=.03 vs full Laplace, >=25% payload savings, and improvement over native subspace/rank-1 controls.
failure_gate: Any quality/storage miss or exact native PCA/subspace function/payload alias => FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Fixed random-feature classifier only; not an end-to-end neural model.
Synthetic data and one development seed only.
No audit, natural benchmark, GPU or deployment calibration claim.
